subject.title: Timeout compaction can report success but leave Codex channel session unrecoverable

question: After repeated timeout compactions on a Codex-backed channel session, should OpenClaw automatically roll over the persistent session, or should it fail clearly and require an explicit user/operator reset?
rationale: Automatic rollover can recover stuck chat lanes but may discard or hide meaningful session context and tool-side-effect uncertainty; the source-level bug is clear, but the durable recovery policy is a product decision.

options.title: Fail clearly before auto-rollover
options.body: Keep the current session mapping, stop claiming recovery after repeated timeout compactions, and tell the user/operator to run a visible reset path such as `/new` until live proof supports automatic rollover.

options.title: Auto-rollover after capped retries
options.body: Rotate the affected session key to a fresh Codex thread after the timeout-compaction cap, preserving transcript artifacts and warning that prior tool actions may need verification.

options.title: Defer for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open without code changes until a maintainer captures a current-main high-context Discord or Telegram repro that proves the safest recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Fail clearly before auto-rollover
recommendation.body: Keep the current session mapping, stop claiming recovery after repeated timeout compactions, and tell the user/operator to run a visible reset path such as `/new` until live proof supports automatic rollover.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent app-server completion-stall recovery work is closest to the remaining policy surface for incomplete Codex turns and channel-session recovery.
